LESSON: BELIEF IN

Grade: PP2
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: PILLARS
Topic 2.1: Belief in

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Belief in. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: What else has He a) identify oneself and immediate environment through created?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya
3. practise Belief in in clear steps
4. apply Belief in in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: BELIEF IN
Subject: ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Belief in helps you succeed in ISLAMIC RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: BELIEF IN
Study Belief in like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Belief in” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Belief in in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Belief in in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Belief in in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Belief in in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Belief in in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Belief in in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Belief in in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Belief in in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Belief in” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Belief in in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Belief in is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Belief in” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Belief in in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Belief in in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Belief in” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Belief in in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Belief in to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Belief in in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Belief in from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Belief in: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Belief in?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What else has He a) identify oneself and immediate environment through created?
2. How are we different Creation as stated in the Qur’an • Learners to sing simple Islamic songs from animals?
3. How do we take care of others of oneself and others as related to the strand. Allah’s creation?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Belief in means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Belief in means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Belief in from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
